To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the implementation of a comprehensive psychological services program in a breast cancer unit is feasible and that such a program can be beneficial to the patients and their families, as well as to the staff.
the implementation of psychosocial programs in a comprehensive breast cancer program is feasible and can be effective.

the implementation of psychosocial programs for the patient and family, and for the staff, in the inpatient and outpatient settings, and for the visiting nursing staff in the home, is a crucial element in the management of emotional stress in breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the implementation of psychosocial care for breast cancer patients, and we are currently in the process of developing a model for comprehensive psychosocial care in breast cancer patients, based on the needs of the patients, their families and the staff.

the development of comprehensive psychosocial services which can be implemented in a variety of health care settings, and which can be used to provide support for patients and their families, as well as for the health care professionals who work with them.
the development of a model for the delivery of psychosocial support to the breast cancer patient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the psychosocial care of the breast cancer patient requires the integration of the services of a variety of disciplines, including nursing, social work, psychiatry, psychology, pastoral counseling, and Reach‐to‐recovery.
the psychosocial needs of breast cancer patients and their families are great and that these needs are not being met by the current health care system.

the implementation of psychological services in the treatment of breast cancer patients requires a team approach, with a balance among services which are available to the patients and their families, and to the staff, with a special emphasis upon the needs of the staff.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the emotional needs of the breast cancer patient and family are met by an integrated program which includes the patient, her family, the nursing and medical staff, and community support.
a combination of the above elements in the three settings is necessary to meet the needs of the breast cancer patient and the staff.
a team approach, including the patient, her physician and nurse, and the patient's family, is the best way to provide emotional support and to manage emotional stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a comprehensive approach to the psychological needs of the patient and the family, and to the staff in the inpatient and outpatient settings, is necessary.
the provision of psychological services to the breast cancer patient and her family must include the provision of services for the staff.
a team approach is necessary for the provision of psychosocial care for breast cancer patients.
